latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Excess open probability or abnormal regulation of skeletal-muscle calcium release channels creates uncontrolled myoplasmic calcium after a compatible activating context in a susceptible host.
Uncontrolled calcium cycling produces masseter spasm, generalized rigidity or contracture, high ATP consumption, muscle heat generation, and early myocyte stress.
Skeletal muscle ATP turnover and oxygen consumption accelerate, causing rapidly rising CO2 production, hypercapnia despite ventilation, tachycardia, tachypnea, and hyperthermia.

CO2 retention, lactic acid production, ATP depletion, cell membrane injury, potassium release, calcium shifts, and renal impairment create mixed acidosis, hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, and arrhythmia vulnerability.
Sustained contracture, heat, ATP depletion, and membrane injury release CK, myoglobin, potassium, LDH, AST, and ALT, with myoglobinuria and pigment nephropathy risk.

Hypercapnia, acidosis, hyperkalemia, catecholamine stress, vasodilation, anesthetic exposure, and myocardial oxygen demand create hypertension or hypotension, shock, malignant arrhythmia, and ventilation failure risk.

Uncontrolled hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, acidosis, shock, hyperkalemia, hypoxemia, and coagulopathy accumulate into AKI, DIC, acute liver injury, cerebral injury, respiratory failure, recrudescence, and death.

Depolarizing neuromuscular blocker exposure can rapidly amplify abnormal calcium release in susceptible muscle.
Genetic or syndromic susceptibility raises the probability that a compatible exposure enters the malignant hyperthermia vector field.
Removal of activating agents reduces ongoing calcium-release drive.
Myoplasmic calcium excess directly causes contracture and rigidity.
Sustained contraction consumes ATP and oxygen and produces heat and CO2.
CO2 accumulation and lactate production create mixed acidosis and amplify potassium shift.
Contracture and ATP depletion injure myocytes, releasing CK and myoglobin.
Acidosis and potassium shifts destabilize cardiac and ventilatory physiology.
Pigment load, tissue injury, and electrolyte release drive AKI, liver enzyme elevation, and coagulopathy.
Shock, arrhythmia, hypoxemia, and ventilation failure propagate organ injury.
Masseter spasm can be an early manifestation of contracture, especially around airway management.
Sustained calcium-mediated contraction produces rigidity or contracture.
Increased CO2 production often appears as rising EtCO2 despite increased ventilation.
CO2 production can exceed ventilation, raising PaCO2.
Muscle hypermetabolism generates heat; temperature can lag behind EtCO2.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: EtCO2 and PaCO2 are linked by CO2 production and ventilation, with divergence possible during ventilation changes or shock.
Rising CO2 may precede obvious temperature rise.
Heat and catecholamine stress commonly raise heart rate together.
Rigidity and contracture precede CK rise.
Marked CK elevation represents the rhabdomyolysis event pathway.
Myoglobinuria and pigment load raise AKI risk.
Hyperkalemia is a direct arrhythmia driver.
Acidemia potentiates arrhythmia and hemodynamic collapse.
Shock and hypoperfusion raise lactate, but muscle hypermetabolism can raise lactate independently.
Extreme heat and tissue injury can evolve into coagulopathy.
Severe heat injury and shock can precipitate liver injury.
Arrhythmia is one of the fastest death pathways in malignant hyperthermia.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit depends on stopping ongoing volatile exposure.
Residual vapor, circuit contamination, or continued trigger exposure sustains upstream drive.

side_effects.interpretation: Anesthetic transition and vasoactive treatment can destabilize blood pressure.

treatments.context_specific_role: Removes the observed activating context and enables all other therapies to reshape the calcium-driven crisis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: No adequate drug supply or preparation capacity prevents mechanism-level rescue.
Late treatment allows organ injury to accumulate before calcium release is inhibited.
Dantrolene can cause hepatotoxicity, but acute crisis benefit may dominate with monitoring.

side_effects.interpretation: Therapeutic effect can cause generalized weakness after crisis control.
Hepatic enzyme monitoring is relevant during repeated dosing or liver vulnerability.

treatments.context_specific_role: Direct mechanism-level inhibitor of abnormal skeletal-muscle calcium release during the acute vector field.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hypercarbia is directly targeted by ventilation and high fresh gas flow.
Severe shock can impair EtCO2 interpretation and oxygen delivery despite ventilation.

side_effects.interpretation: High intrathoracic pressure or deep anesthesia can lower venous return.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapidly controls hypercarbia and oxygen delivery while upstream calcium and trigger mechanisms are controlled.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cooling benefit grows as temperature rises.
Cooling is weaker when untreated muscle contracture continues generating heat.

side_effects.interpretation: Cooling can trigger shivering unless anesthesia or sedation suppresses it.

treatments.context_specific_role: Direct state push lowering temperature and thermal event hazard while dantrolene and trigger removal stop heat production.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe acidemia destabilizes myocardium and worsens potassium shift.

side_effects.interpretation: Calcium salts can transiently raise measured calcium while stabilizing myocardium.

treatments.context_specific_role: Prevents arrhythmia and shock pathways while rhabdomyolysis and calcium-release mechanisms are treated.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Higher pigment load increases renal-protection value.
Fluid can worsen pulmonary edema or oxygenation.

side_effects.interpretation: Excess fluid can worsen pulmonary edema in vulnerable patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supports perfusion and pigment clearance after the upstream calcium crisis is controlled.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Catecholamines can worsen arrhythmia risk while supporting shock.

side_effects.interpretation: Catecholamines may increase arrhythmia susceptibility in acidemic or hyperkalemic patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Perfusion support for shock physiology while definitive mechanism control is applied.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Dialysis or CRRT directly treats refractory hyperkalemia.
CRRT is often better tolerated than intermittent dialysis during shock.

side_effects.interpretation: Intermittent dialysis or ultrafiltration can worsen hypotension.
Catheter placement and anticoagulation can add bleeding risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Organ support for refractory electrolyte, acid-base, volume, and AKI consequences after severe rhabdomyolysis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Ongoing observation and repeated rescue reduce missed recurrence.
Delayed rhabdomyolysis and electrolyte injury require serial monitoring.

sigma_modulation.clinical_rationale: Continuous ICU monitoring and rapid rescue reduce uncontrolled volatility.

side_effects.interpretation: ICU care may involve ventilation exposure, but monitoring also reduces preventable death risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Controls delayed hazards after the acute crisis, especially recrudescence, CK/myoglobin peak, potassium rebound, AKI, and arrhythmia.

supportive_care: Preserve the exact anesthesia and medication chronology as context: agents, doses when reported, timing from induction or recovery, ventilation settings, EtCO2 trend, temperature site, and when treatment started.

Use presentation physiology as ordinary ranking evidence: unexplained EtCO2 rise, arterial PaCO2, pH, base excess, lactate, temperature, tachycardia, rigidity or masseter spasm, potassium, CK, myoglobin, creatinine, AST/ALT/LDH, urine color, and organ support needs.

Store Larach clinical grading score, final paper diagnosis, genetic testing, caffeine-halothane contracture testing, and dramatic dantrolene response as confirmatory or context evidence with use_in_ranking:false in case JSON.
Do not treat antipyretics as causal therapy; temperature is driven by skeletal muscle hypermetabolism and requires trigger removal, dantrolene, cooling, ventilation, and metabolic support.
Trend CK and myoglobin after initial control because the rhabdomyolysis peak can lag behind EtCO2 and temperature control.
Monitor and treat hyperkalemia, acidemia, hypocalcemia, hypoglycemia after insulin, renal injury, arrhythmia, DIC/coagulopathy, liver injury, and respiratory failure.
Continue ICU-level observation after apparent control for recurrence, potassium rebound, delayed AKI, and delayed CK/myoglobin peak.
After recovery, document malignant hyperthermia susceptibility precautions, family counseling context, and future anesthesia avoidance of triggering agents outside ordinary presentation ranking.
